subject: Migration mode selection: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T16:10:00Z
Subject: Migration mode selection: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (post-call recap)

Hi Peter —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment. Please reply with comments or confirm.

Summary of Lumina's constraints we captured:
- Current stack: in-production LLM features running on Anthropic API and some self-hosted models on legacy GPU cluster for fine-tuned workloads.
- Migration drivers: reliability & latency in region, predictable unit economics, and tighter data controls for PII flows.
- Compliance: SOC 2 evidence and contractual audit access will be required across prod and staging.

Redwood deployment options we discussed (high level):
1) Hosted API — fastest go-live, usage-based pricing, good for bursty traffic and POC. Less control over dedicated capacity and some limitations for strict data residency.
2) Dedicated — reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and isolation (can backstop live traffic while migrating). Works well if you need consistent latency and lower unit cost at scale.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — full network isolation and customer-managed infra for regulated data; longer procurement and onboarding.

Preliminary recommendation for Lumina (based on call):
- Start with Dedicated capacity for core inference (predictable performance) while keeping non-sensitive workloads on Hosted API during cutover.
- Evaluate Private VPC in parallel if legal/regulatory requires on-prem or strict network controls.

Proposed next steps:
- Internal tech deep-dive (1 hour) with Dev to validate runtime compatibility and KV cache migration patterns. (Action: schedule)
- Lumina to share a short list of top 3 latency-sensitive endpoints and expected QPS / token mix. (Action: Peter)
- We'll provide a migration playbook + SOC 2 excerpt and a Dedicated pricing tear sheet. (Action: Marissa / Dev)

Can you confirm availability for a technical call next week (we have slots Tue/Wed 11–3 PT)?

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Migration mode selection: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (post-call recap)

Hi Peter —

Quick answers to your bullets + attached artifacts.

1) Autoscaling and burst handling for Dedicated:
- Dedicated supports configured autoscaling policies (scale up/down on target queue latency and token throughput). Burst capacity can be reserved as part of the committed plan or allowed to overflow to Hosted (policy-based fallback).
- Cold-starts: KV cache warmup is handled via prefix cache preloading and background warming on new instances; for stateful fine-tuned models we recommend a small pre-warm pool to minimize tail latency on scale events.

2) Compliance & logs:
- SOC 2 artifact attached (soc2-excerpt.pdf). We provide audit logs, key management integrations (KMS), and optional timeline for evidence collection for procurement.

3) Migration approach (high level):
- Phase 1: Pilot — route 20% traffic to Dedicated, keep user-facing on Hosted as fallback.
- Phase 2: Gradual shift — incrementally raise Dedicated traffic while validating metrics (latency, error rate, cost).
- Phase 3: Cutover & optionally enable Private VPC for regulated workloads post-contract.

Attaching: redwood_migration_playbook.pdf (detailed steps), dedicated-pricing-tearsheet.xlsx (example tiers).

I’ll also bring a short checklist to the call on Tue to walk through token mix, model variants, and any inference-specific constraints (quantization/FP16 support).

Best,
Dev Patel
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
